configurePresets.name: linux-x64-gcc
configurePresets.description: GCC for x64 Linux: native on x64 hardware; on an ARM64 machine a cross build with x86_64-linux-gnu-g++

configurePresets.name: linux-x64-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang for x64 Linux: native on x64 hardware; on an ARM64 machine a cross build (clang++ --target=x86_64-linux-gnu)

configurePresets.name: linux-arm64-gcc
configurePresets.description: GCC for ARM64 (aarch64) Linux: native on ARM64 hardware, otherwise a cross build with aarch64-linux-gnu-g++ (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install g++-aarch64-linux-gnu; qemu-user, if installed, lets ctest run the result)

configurePresets.name: linux-arm64-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang for ARM64 (aarch64) Linux: native on ARM64 hardware, otherwise a cross build (clang++ --target=aarch64-linux-gnu; needs the aarch64 GCC cross package for its libraries, or -DCMAKE_SYSROOT)

configurePresets.name: linux-arm32-gcc
configurePresets.description: GCC for 32-bit ARM (armhf) Linux: native on 32-bit ARM hardware, otherwise a cross build with arm-linux-gnueabihf-g++ (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install g++-arm-linux-gnueabihf). A 32-bit ARM userland on 64-bit ARM hardware should pass -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++ -- see breeze/cmake/toolchains/_common.cmake

configurePresets.name: linux-arm32-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang for 32-bit ARM (armhf) Linux: native on 32-bit ARM hardware, otherwise a cross build (clang++ --target=<the triple the cross g++ was built for, normally arm-linux-gnueabihf>) -- see linux-arm32-gcc

configurePresets.name: macos-arm64-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang for Apple Silicon macOS -- Apple Clang from the Xcode Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install), or LLVM's own with -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER. The architecture is pinned with CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES, so this means arm64 even under a Rosetta-translated cmake; minimum macOS 11.0

configurePresets.name: macos-x64-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang for Intel macOS -- Apple Clang from the Xcode Command Line Tools, or LLVM's own with -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER. Pinned to x86_64 with CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES, so on an Apple Silicon Mac it builds x64 code that runs through Rosetta 2; minimum macOS 11.0

configurePresets.name: windows-x64-msvc
configurePresets.description: cl.exe for x64: run from an x64 Native Tools Command Prompt for VS -- cl.exe's architecture comes from that developer environment, not from CMake

configurePresets.name: windows-arm64-msvc
configurePresets.description: cl.exe for ARM64: run from a Visual Studio Developer Prompt configured for ARM64 (an ARM64 Native Tools prompt, or x64_arm64 via vcvarsall.bat to cross-build from an x64 host) -- cl.exe's architecture comes from that environment, not from CMake

configurePresets.name: windows-x64-clang-cl
configurePresets.description: clang-cl (Clang with the MSVC ABI), pinned to --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc so it means x64 whatever the machine's own architecture is

configurePresets.name: windows-arm64-clang-cl
configurePresets.description: clang-cl (Clang with the MSVC ABI), pinned to --target=aarch64-pc-windows-msvc so it means ARM64 whatever the machine's own architecture is

configurePresets.name: windows-x64-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang with its own GNU-style driver, e.g. from an MSYS2 CLANG64 shell -- assumes that environment's clang++ is what's on PATH, distinct from clang-cl above

configurePresets.name: windows-arm64-clang
configurePresets.description: Clang with its own GNU-style driver, e.g. from an MSYS2 CLANGARM64 shell -- assumes that environment's clang++ is what's on PATH

configurePresets.name: windows-x86-mingw32
configurePresets.description: 32-bit MinGW g++: i686-w64-mingw32-g++ from an MSYS2 MINGW32 shell on Windows, or a cross build from Linux (apt install g++-mingw-w64-i686; wine, if installed, lets ctest run the result)

configurePresets.name: windows-x64-mingw64
configurePresets.description: 64-bit MinGW-w64 g++: x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ from an MSYS2 MINGW64 shell on Windows, or a cross build from Linux (apt install g++-mingw-w64-x86-64; wine, if installed, lets ctest run the result)
